brief: Zero-knowledge encrypted pastebin. First screen = compose a secret, seal it, hand over a one-time link. Every candidate keeps the same core task: name (optional), payload, retention, optional passphrase, one primary action that encrypts and returns a share link.

candidates.name: Current UI (Spotify-terminal)
candidates.concept: Dark hacker terminal with Spotify green — the look the user says feels copied.
candidates.typography: DM Sans / Figtree / JetBrains Mono, geometric sans hierarchy
traits: three feature cards above the form

candidates.name: 01 · Dead Drop
candidates.concept: Using the site feels like filing a document at a covert dead drop: a case-file form on manila paper, sealed with a rubber stamp, issued a disposal receipt.
candidates.typography: Special Elite (typewriter) for content, Oswald caps for labels, Saira Stencil One for stamps; inputs are ink underlines, no boxes
traits: rotated stamp as the primary action

candidates.name: 02 · Sanctum
candidates.concept: Using the site feels like entering a candlelit order: one vellum slip in a vast darkness, and encrypting presses a wax seal — spoken once, then silence.
candidates.typography: Cormorant Garamond for voice, IBM Plex Mono only for data; hairline rules on vellum
traits: warm black with candle glow, no panels
the action is a wax seal, not a button
serif on paper — no terminal anywhere

candidates.name: 03 · Wire
candidates.concept: Using the site feels like operating a silent dispatch desk: a numbered industrial grid, and a live SERVER VIEW strip shows the black bars of noise your transmission actually becomes.
candidates.typography: Oswald condensed caps for the masthead and stencil tags, IBM Plex Mono for all content; square corners, 1.5px ink borders
traits: bright industrial grid — breaks the dark-hacker cliché
live SERVER VIEW redaction under the payload
parameter blocks as numbered punch-card forms
